subject: Data Engineering
title: Lake Security and Access Control
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Lake Security and Access Control.

hook.text: The data lake contains PII, financial records, and health data all in the same bucket. Who has access?

buildup.text: Lake security combines cloud IAM policies, bucket policies, and data-layer access controls.

discovery.text: Fine-grained access controls restrict users to specific folders, tables, or even columns within the lake.

twist.text: Object storage permissions are coarse. You need a governance layer on top to enforce row and column security.

climax.text: Tools like AWS Lake Formation and Unity Catalog add the governance layer that raw object storage lacks.

punchline.text: The lake holds everything. Governance decides who sees what.

quiz.question: Why do data lakes need a governance layer on top of object storage?
options: Object storage permissions are too coarse for row and column security
Object storage has no permissions at all
